critic: LEAD (independent critic, checked by a second agent)
verdict:
C13 and C15 (page at 9dd229f; pair and screen at 6b5702c): the new page camera is not a usable plate yet. It breaks no hard rule: the sheets and the screen are blank and no text shows.

Its geometry is sound:
- The sheet is a flat A4.
- The corner pins match the mesh exactly. A pinhole reprojection of the sheet reproduces all four to the pixel. Opposite edges are about 763/856 and 1080/1150 px, which is A4 in perspective.
- Nothing in the raw frame is clipped (max 242). 0.6% of graded pixels are below 8/255 in all three channels (1.7% by luma).

Three things stop it working as a plate.

(1) The sheet shades like a cushion, not like paper. pp.sheet(step=0.014) builds a 15x21 grid with use_smooth=True under a Solidify, so the rim normals most likely blend across the last 14 mm cell. edge_tone adds a further 6 mm of darkening round the rim.
- Far right edge: falls from raw about 135 at 20 mm in, to 115-121 at 10 mm, to 11-27 in the last 2 mm. That is darker than the wood beside it.
- Head edge: falls from 135-151 to 79-91 at the edge.
- Lit left edge: flat.
- The right corner becomes a dark rounded wedge. Its corner pin (1975, 520) lands on the wedge tip, about 30 px past the visible paper corner.
A pinned page multiplied by this shading would carry a dark rounded edge and corner, and would read like a tablet or a plastic tray.

(2) The lamp's hot spot is a specular glint of the bulb on the wood, not on the paper. From this camera, the bulb's mirror point lands at about (-0.22, -0.054), which is on the pen. So the brightest, streakiest wood in frame surrounds the pen: raw 133-143, graded 93-98, against paper at raw 150-175. It reads as brushed metal and pulls the eye off the sheet.

(3) The paper is warm in the raw (161,150,135 at centre) but grades to neutral: 149,149,149 at centre, faintly cool on its brighter left third, peaking at about 157/255. On screen it is a grey card, not the slightly warm paper the brief asks for, and dimmer than a fern document insert.

Two framing problems follow from the -40 degree turn:
- Text will run at 33-39 degrees on screen.
- A 16:9 crop of the lower half is about half wood, and the foot corner sits at most 58 px from the crop's bottom edge.

The pair plate has the same cushioned edges, and its pen lies across the left sheet's edge.

The other five cameras (overhead, passport, laptop, push, purses) are still the round-4 renders of 7249565, regraded to A fixed. The code has moved since: 6d658fb raised BOUNCE['spread'] to 3.6, bound the passport on its long edge, cut its coat to 0.08, removed the ring stain and halved the purses haze. Their round-4 notes can only be re-judged after a re-render.

Across the stage, the paper and wood craft is short of fern, and well short of the koi-pond stills' surface finish.
answers:
1. The blank sheet as a plate for a real A4 page: not yet.

What works: the corner pins are accurate to the mesh, and the sheet is planar (stiff=0, SUPPORT cleared, no rest shape), so a homography fits.

What fails is the shading under the pin. Measured on the raw frame along the homography from the pins:
- Far right edge: the rim darkens over its last 12-15 mm. Raw is about 135 at 20 mm, 115-121 at 10 mm, 82-90 at 6 mm and 11-27 in the last 2 mm.
- Head edge: 135-151 at 20 mm, 79-91 at the edge.
- Foot edge: about 20% darker in its last millimetre.
- Lit left edge: stays flat.
- The right corner is a dark rounded wedge.

Two ways to composite, both bad:
- Multiply a page by this luminance and it inherits the rounded dark rim.
- Composite it straight over and the pin's TR corner overhangs the visible paper corner by about 30 px, with nothing in the plate to blend into.

The interior is otherwise clean. No mottle, smudge or texture shows that would fight a page, and the falloff across it is gentle (graded about 155 at mid-left to 120-130 at 20 mm from the right edge).

The paper colour also fails. After the grade it is neutral grey (149,149,149 at centre), not slightly warm, and dim for a document insert (peak about 157, 61% of white).

2. Framing from the foot of the sheet. The foot corner sits at y=1382 of 1440, 58 px (4%) above the bottom edge. In the full frame that is tight but acceptable. As a crop it is not:
- The lower half of the sheet spans x 546-1594, y 474-1382.
- The smallest 16:9 crop that holds it is about 1614x908: a 1.59x upscale for 1440p and 1.19x for 1080p, with the foot corner on the crop's bottom edge.
- Running the crop down to the frame's bottom (about 1717x966, 1.49x and 1.12x) still leaves the foot corner only 58 px (6%) clear.
- About half of either crop is wood (52-57%).
- Because of the -40 degree turn, the page's lines run at 33 degrees at the head and 39 at the foot.

Resolution alone would survive: about 3.8-4.2 px/mm on the lower half, so a 10-11 pt x-height (about 2 mm) comes out near 9 px at 1080p. But it will not look like a deliberate insert. Use a real second camera on the lower half at native 2560 instead of a crop (fix 4), and cut the turn to about -15 to -20 degrees.

3. The focus change, on the still. fx_page sits 55 mm toward the camera from the sheet centre, in the sheet's lower-left quarter (sheet-local about -35, -42 mm), at f/5.6, 50 mm, about 0.85 m.

Computed blur circles at 2560 px:
- about 1 px at the foot-left corner
- 2.5 px at the foot-right
- 3 px at the head-right
- 5 px at the head-left

The measured left edge agrees: 10-90% edge widths of 1.4-2.7 px from y 300 to 720, and 3.0-3.3 px toward the head (y 140-225). That is a gentle, believable falloff, right for a lower-half shot.

But nothing in the delivery lets the compositor match it. A flat pinned page will be uniformly sharp over a softening sheet. Export the defocus with the corners (fix 5), or the head of the pinned page will look pasted on. I can only judge the static frame. If "focus change" means an animated pull, no frames of it were delivered.

4. The paper-to-wood edge: clean on the lit side, wrong on the far side.

The lit edges (upper left and the left corner) are crisp, 1.4-3.3 px, with no line or catch. That is what a 0.22 mm sheet does at 0.85 m. But beside the left corner the wood is the glint (raw 110-117 against paper at 165-173), so that corner has little contrast and looks laid on.

The far right edge shows no separate contact shadow. Instead the paper's own last 2-4 mm go near black (raw 11-27, darker than the wood beside it), and that reads as a thick dark rim. The head edge falls to raw 80-90. The foot is only mildly darkened. The right corner is a dark rounded wedge instead of a crisp paper corner.

5. Pen and highlighter. In the full frame, the pen pulls more attention than the highlighter:
- It sits exactly in the bulb's specular glint on the wood. The bulb's mirror point projects to about (358, 872), on the pen, in the brightest, streakiest wood in frame.
- Its chrome band near the tip is the brightest pixel in the frame (raw 242).

The highlighter is the only hue in the frame: graded about 54,51,29, up to 73,69,43 on its lit side. That is a khaki that reads as a glue stick, not a highlighter. It stands alone on the right third, so it is a second stop for the eye.

In a lower-half crop the highlighter (x about 2246-2362) is out. The pen (x 275-420) sits at the left edge of a crop centred on the lower half and leaves only if the crop slides right.

What to do: keep the highlighter only if it reads as one and belongs to the sheet (fix 7). Take the pen out of the glint: fix 2 removes the glint and fix 7 moves the pen.

6. The other two plates.

The two-sheet camera (pair.jpg) shows the same build fault:
- Both sheets darken over their last 12-15 mm on the right and foot edges. On the left sheet's right edge, raw is 64-74 at the edge against 155-166 at 20 mm. On the right sheet's right edge, 10-21 against 119-126.
- The foot-right corners are dark and rounded.
- The lamp-base arc shows top left.
- Its pen lies across the left sheet's left edge near mid-height, covering 6-8 mm of paper, so a page pinned there would need a matte.
Fix the shared sheet build and move the pen before re-rendering it.

The laptop screen plate (screen.jpg):
- It has a blotchy lighter band on the inner edge of both side bezels, not just the left.
- screen.png is 1280x720, not 2560x1440 like page and pair, and it has no corners file (frame_metadata covers only page and pair). It is not yet a plate like the other two.

fixes.problem:
The blank sheet shades like a cushion. pp.sheet(..., step=0.014) gives a 15x21 grid that place_flat smooth-shades under a Solidify, so the normals at the rim most likely tilt outward across the last 14 mm cell. edge_tone=(0.21, 0.297) darkens a further 6 mm all round.

Measured on the raw along the homography from the pins:
- Far right edge: falls from about 135 at 15-20 mm in, to 115-121 at 10 mm, 82-90 at 6 mm, and 11-27 in the last 2 mm. That is darker than the wood beside it.
- Head edge: falls from 135-151 to 79-91.
- Foot edge: about 80% at the edge.
- Lit left edge: flat (the tilt's brightening is cancelled by edge_tone).

The right corner is a dark rounded wedge, and the TR pin (1975, 520) lands on its tip, about 30 px past the visible paper corner. A pinned page multiplied by this shading would inherit all of it.
fixes.fix:
1. In document_plates(), after each pp.sheet(...) returns ob, add `for p in ob.data.polygons: p.use_smooth = False`. The sheet is planar, so nothing is lost. The Solidify already builds its rim by default; no other modifier setting is needed.
2. Give the plate sheets their own material without edge_tone: `mt.paper('plate paper', (0.80, 0.74, 0.60), 0.88, fibre=0.02, smudge=0.0, translucency=0.10, edge_tone=None)`.

Check on the raw frame:
- Along each edge, luma 3 mm inside the paper is within 5% of luma 20 mm inside.
- The right corner is a sharp point.
- The TR pin falls within 2 px of the visible paper corner.

If flat shading alone does not clear the band, the cause is elsewhere in the rim. Mark the boundary edges sharp, or drop the Solidify for these plates, and re-check.

fixes.problem:
The brightest wood in frame is a specular glint of the bulb, not the pool.
- With the page lamp mark (-0.40, 0.20, -123), the bulb sits at about (-0.34, 0.16, TOP+0.41).
- Its mirror point from this camera is about (-0.22, -0.054), which projects to (358, 872), on the pen.
- The wood there reads raw 133-143 with brushed-metal streaks (graded 93-98), close to the paper's raw 150-175.
- Wood nearer the pool's centre, above the sheet's left corner, reads only 65-76.
- The table wood's roughness is 0.46.
The eye goes to the pen, not the sheet.
fixes.fix:
Scope every change to the plate cameras only: page, pair and the new page_foot. Motifs and visa share the 'document' beat and must not change.

1. In apply_camera(), set visible_glossy = False on lamp_spot, lamp_glow and the lamp_bulb mesh, and restore True for every other camera. Alternatively, raise table_top's roughness by about 0.25 for these cameras only.
2. Give the plates their own beat, so their level can change without touching motifs and visa: HIDE['plate'] = DOCUMENT_PROPS, beat='plate' on page and pair, and LAMP_LEVEL['plate'] about 1.35-1.5.
3. Leave BOUNCE at its 1.6 default. Lowering it would sink the corners further.

Targets on the graded frame:
- Paper peak about 185-200 on the sheet's upper-left third, with raw paper under about 235.
- Wood beside the pen no brighter than about half the paper beside it (now 93-98 against 140-158).
- Wood at the frame corners 12-20, above 8. The top-right corner is 5-7 now.

fixes.problem: The paper is warm in the raw (R/B 1.16-1.24; 161,150,135 at centre), but grade A fixed turns it neutral: 149,149,149 at centre, and R-B -1.5 to -2 on the brighter left third. The brief asks for matt, slightly warm paper. With a graded peak of about 157 (61%), it reads as a grey card.
fixes.fix:
Warm the raw so the warmth survives saturation 0.55 and the shadow cooling. Use the plate-paper rgb from fix 1, (0.80, 0.74, 0.60), aiming for a raw R/B of about 1.35-1.40 at the sheet centre.

Check on the graded frame: centre R-B at +6 to +10 and G-B at +3 to +5.

For the comp: multiply the real page by the blank sheet's normalised luminance and composite it into a copy of the raw plate. Then grade that copy with the same GRADE filter from shoot.py (the ffmpeg line in regrade_frames.sh). That way the page takes the same falloff, warmth and vignette.

fixes.problem:
Because of the -40 degree turn, text runs at 33-39 degrees on screen. A 16:9 crop of the lower half:
- is about half wood (52-57%)
- needs a 1.49-1.59x upscale for 1440p
- leaves the foot corner 0-6% from the crop's bottom edge
Cropping is the wrong way to make that shot.
fixes.fix:
1. Change document_single's turn from -40 to -18, so text runs at 14-17 degrees.
2. The page camera can stay where it is: the whole sheet then has about 9% margin at the top and 6% at the bottom. Or pull it back along its line to loc=(0.0, -0.47, TOP+0.785), aim unchanged, for about 10% and 8%.
3. Add a dedicated camera, with the same viewing direction brought in to 0.40 m: CAMERAS['page_foot'] = dict(CAMERAS['page'], loc=(-0.02, -0.306, TOP+0.346), aim=(-0.02, -0.105, TOP), lens=50, focus='fx_page_foot', fstop=8.0, show=('page sheet',)), with empty('fx_page_foot', (-0.02, -0.105, TOP + 0.0003)).
4. Add 'page_foot': ('document_single',) to frame_metadata's names, so it writes its own corners. The head corners will be off-frame.

What the projection gives (pinhole, 36 mm sensor, which reproduces the published pins exactly):
- Foot corners at about (157, 749) and (2000, 1297): 10% above the bottom edge and 6% from the left.
- Paper fills about 52% of the frame, at about 9 px/mm.
- Blur is about 3-4 px at the two foot corners at f/8. At f/4.5 it would be 5-7 px, too soft.

Check on the render: both foot corners are inside the frame, at least 8% above the bottom edge and 5% from the sides.

fixes.problem: The depth of field (f/5.6, about 0.85 m, focused on the lower-left quarter) softens the head of the sheet: edge widths of 3.0-3.3 px near the head, against 1.4-2.7 px mid-edge. Computed blur circles are about 1 px at the foot-left corner, 2.5 at the foot-right, 3 at the head-right and 5 at the head-left. But the plate does not tell the compositor any of this. A flat pinned page will be uniformly sharp over a softening sheet.
fixes.fix:
In frame_metadata(), add to each page entry 'depth_m' per corner (the distance from the camera to each corner's world point). Add top-level 'focus_m' (the distance to fx_page), plus 'fstop', 'lens_mm' and 'sensor_mm' from scene.camera.data.

Alternatively, write a 16-bit Z pass (view_layer.use_pass_z, normalised to the sheet's depth range) next to page.png, so the comp can blur the pinned page by the same circle of confusion.

Better still, also deliver an f/11 'page_sharp' render for the pin, and add the depth of field in comp.

fixes.problem:
The paper-to-wood edge does not read as paper on a table.
- Lit side: the edge is crisp (1.4-3.3 px), with no line or catch. That is what a 0.22 mm sheet does at 0.85 m. But beside the left corner the wood is the glint (raw 110-117 against paper at 165-173), so that corner has little contrast and looks laid on.
- Far side: there is no visible contact shadow. The paper's own last 2-4 mm go near black (see the first fix), which reads as a thick dark rim.
fixes.fix:
No bevel. At about 3.9 px/mm, a 0.08 mm bevel is a third of a pixel and cannot make a 1 px line.

After the shading fix and the glint fix, check:
- Far right and head edges: the sheet's top is 0.28 mm above the wood (0.22 mm Solidify plus the 0.06 mm gap). The lamp, at about 40 degrees elevation, should throw a 0.3 mm (about 1 px) contact shadow onto the wood there.
- Lit left corner: the paper should stand clear of the wood by at least 2:1 in raw luma.

If a little life is wanted, lift the two head corners with shape=pp.sheet_shape(0.21, 0.297, 1, corners=(0, 0, 0.0005, 0.0003), wave=0.0). The default wave of 0.0006 would cockle the plate. Then re-export the corners; the lift moves the head pins by under 2 px.

fixes.problem:
Props and set noise outside the paper:
- The highlighter is the only hue (graded about 54,51,29, a khaki that reads as a glue stick) and stands alone on the right third.
- The pen sits in the glint.
- A pale double arc in the top-left corner (raw x 0-110, y 0-150) is the rim of the lamp's round base. The base's centre projects just outside the frame, at about (-176, 53). The arc reads as a stray cable.
- White diagonal scratches in the top wood catch the eye.
- The plank end-joint at the top left, with its rounded bevels, reads as floor decking.
fixes.fix:
Highlighter: give the page's highlighter its own group so it can differ from the pair's. Either leave it out of 'page', or, with the -18 degree sheet, lay it on the wood along the sheet's far right edge, parallel to it and about 30 mm off the paper, at about (0.14, -0.015) turned 72. That spot projects whole inside the page frame (x about 1800-1920, y 535-940). It cannot share the pair's group, because that spot is under document_right. If it stays, give it its own brighter, more saturated body (raw about 190,170,40) and check on the graded frame that it reads yellow, not khaki.

Pen: after the glint fix, move it to about (-0.26, 0.02) turned 80. It projects whole inside both the page and pair frames and clears the pair's left sheet by about 70 px.

Lamp-base arc: for page and pair, set visible_camera = False on the lamp's meshes. The lamp is out of frame in both, and its lights are separate objects.

Wood: for these cameras, halve the scratch layers on the table wood. Keep the plank end-joints away from the sheet: with the -18 degree turn, the head-left corner is 0.12 m from board 2's end-joint at x = -0.17. Moving the sheet, its props, fx_page and the cameras 0.05 m in +x clears that to 0.17 m.

fixes.problem:
The same sheet build.
- Both sheets darken over their last 12-15 mm on the right and foot edges. On the left sheet, raw is 64-74 at the edge against 155-166 at 20 mm. On the right sheet's right edge, 10-21 against 119-126.
- The foot-right corners are dark and rounded.
- The pen lies across the left sheet's left edge near mid-height, covering 6-8 mm of paper, so a pinned page would need a matte.
- The lamp-base arc shows top left.
- The highlighter again stands alone at the right edge.
fixes.fix:
Apply the shading, glint and warm-paper fixes to document_left and document_right. Move the pen to (-0.26, 0.02, 80) as in the props fix, and hide the lamp meshes from the camera. Then re-render the pair and re-export pair.corners.json.

Check:
- Luma 3 mm inside each edge of both sheets is within 5% of luma 20 mm inside.
- No prop overlaps either sheet's pinned quad.

fixes.problem: The published screen plate (6b5702c) is 1280x720, not 2560x1440 like page and pair. It has no corners file, because frame_metadata covers only page and pair, so the screen cannot be pinned from data. A blotchy lighter band runs along the inner edge of both side bezels (x about 315-330 and 965-980 in the 1280 frame).
fixes.fix: Add final_res=(2560, 1440) to CAMERAS['screen']. Add 'screen' to frame_metadata with the laptop screen panel's four corners. Re-render, then check the bezel band at full size: the bezel next to the panel should be an even dark edge.

fixes.problem:
This frame is still the round-4 render (7249565).
- The top and right third fall to 8-12/255 (45% of the top fifth is under 8).
- The passport reads as a slate tile (graded about 73,77,84).
- The pen lies across the trifold letter, which will carry a composited page.
Since then, 6d658fb raised BOUNCE['spread'] from 2.0 to 3.6, bound the passport on its long edge and cut its cover's Coat Weight from 0.2 to 0.08. Those changes target the first two problems.
fixes.fix:
Re-render overhead from HEAD before judging the bounce and cover changes. Passport, laptop and push are also round-4 renders and need the same.

If the far wood still grades under 8, add a weak warm area light (about 0.6 x 0.4 m, 3 W) 1 m above (0.35, 0.15), light-linked to the table, until the wood grades 12-20.

Move 'pen' in spread() off the letter so the letter's composite needs no matte. The pen sits at (0.25, -0.29), inside the outline of the letter at (0.31, -0.205), turn -14.

fixes.problem: Still the round-4 render: the ring stain on the front plank reads as a dark scratch crescent, and the burgundy bag sits in a lit haze bank.
fixes.fix:
6d658fb already changes both in code:
- The ring at (-0.22, -0.235) is gone from the table wood's rings.
- apply_camera sets the table air to 0.006 for purses (0.013 elsewhere).
Re-render purses and check that the haze at the left edge reads raw 30 or below, with the burgundy bag's folds readable.
